title: a remote box's database is a cache and backup of the master: a local read of a node or tree that is not local is filled from the master by row number
intention: A remote box keeps its own database as a CACHE AND BACKUP of the master's. A node's id is its MASTER ROW NUMBER and nothing else. A local db read of a node or tree that is not local is fed from the master and the local copy is populated at the same time. A row number the box has been handed or has seen but not yet fetched is a NOTCACHED placeholder, and a node's state is VOID, NOTCACHED, or its data.
why: Akien 2026-11-14, answering Q#104 (relayed by the orchestrator, verbatim): "the code is wrong. there shall be no data node ids based on anything other than master row number." and "we need a TESTING database. the sync is the backup. if a local db call is made and that node or tree is not local, it's fed from the master and the local is also populated, so the local is a cache (and backup)... Gap rows are marked NOTCACHED. Node states: VOID / NOTCACHED / <data>." That reverses the sync-3ef8 build (content-hash ids, a primary-key union pushed from home) and reshapes the sync from a copy job into a read-through cache: nothing is copied until something asks for it. Measured 2026-11-12: akienasus's local db held none of codemother's trees while akiendelllinux's held 688 rows, so 2b3d842bc118's clause 4 reds on akienasus.
traces_to: outline 4.3.1.5.1.1 (a row number is the same on every box; slots reserved from the home librarian, gaps held as blanks) and 11.3.5.1 (the local copy is fast, the sync is the backup), Law 6 (the master assigns, the owner gates).
how: D1 (waits for the librarian's row-id ticket, akiendelllinux): the id of a node is the integer the master librarian reserved; no function of content makes an id. D2: db_domain's cache path in sync.py: read_through(table, row_number): the local row is data -> return it; NOTCACHED or absent -> ask the master over the bus (the master's db_domain answers a `fetch` verb for one row or one tree), write the answer locally through the owner gate, return it; VOID on the master -> the local row records VOID and nothing else is made up. D3: a slot handed to this box that it does not hold is written NOTCACHED, never left absent (4.3.1.5.1.1's blanks). D4: the backup half: a local write goes to the master by reservation first (the slot comes from the master), and a local row the master lacks is pushed (the master stays the one assigner). D5: the transport is the bus verb, not a database link; the testing database (a separate ticket) is what a proof runs against.

clauses.claim: a local read of a node row number the box does not hold is answered from the master and the local table then holds it, identical, under the same owner
a row number handed to the box and not yet fetched reads NOTCACHED locally, and reads as data after the first read-through
a row the master marks VOID is cached as VOID and a second read does not ask the master again
no node id on either box is derived from content: two nodes with the same content hold two row numbers

decisions.text: D1: the cache path, replacing sync.py's insert-only union.
D2: the proof, two real databases (the master and a cache) on the testing database's rules, one tooth per clause 1-4.
